title: Tenant-aware cost visibility and SLO management PRD
author: Maya Chen
body:
Overview:

This PRD describes a new product feature set: tenant-aware cost visibility and SLO management. The goal is to give customers and internal teams precise per-tenant (or per-project) attribution for inference spend, resource utilization, and SLO performance while preserving the low-latency, cost-efficient serving characteristics of Redwood. The scope includes API/Console surfaced reports, alerting and automated policy hooks for remediation (rate limits, adaptive routing), and a minimal billing integration to enable new pricing bundles.

Why this matters:
- Customers require stronger cost and quality observability when migrating production workloads to Dedicated or Private deployments.
- Platform teams need deterministic tenant-level SLOs tied to billing and capacity decisions.
- Clear tenant-level telemetry unlocks new pricing products (per-tenant committed capacity, burst credits, quality-tiered bundles).

Goals (success criteria):
1. Provide a console and API that surface daily and rolling-30-day per-tenant breakdowns for tokens, embedding units, and inference wall time.
2. Surface tenant-specific SLOs (p50/p95 latency, error-rate, throughput vs. committed capacity) and enable tenant-scoped alerts when thresholds are breached.
3. Allow product rules to automatically apply remediation policies (degrade to cheaper variant, throttle, or move to fallback region) with traceable audit logs.
4. Ship a lightweight billing export schema for downstream invoicing that contains tenant attribution keys and metering units.
5. Keep added tail-latency overhead < 5 ms on control-plane operations and add no more than 2% cost to serving control-plane telemetry.

Non-goals:
- Full general ledger billing replacement. This feature emits metered exports; finance will continue to ingest and reconcile with existing billing pipelines.
- Fine-grained per-token semantic cost attribution (e.g., prompt-specific chargebacks) in the first phase.

Personas and user stories:
- ML Platform Engineer: "I need to verify a customer’s canary rollout is within its committed throughput and not exceeding billable burst credit."
- Product Manager (customer): "I want a daily email summarizing which features caused cost spikes and whether our SLOs dipped."
- Account Executive: "I want a summary CSV I can attach to invoices showing committed vs. actual usage for each tenant."

Functional requirements:
- R1: Per-tenant telemetry capture. The runtime must emit an aggregation record per-tenant per-minute containing: tokens_in, tokens_out, embedding_units, avg_latency_ms, p95_latency_ms, error_count, successful_requests, model_variant, region, and capacity_class.
- R2: Console dashboards. New pages under Console > Billing & SLOs: (a) Tenant Summary, (b) SLO Heatmap, (c) Cost Drivers (top prompts / routes by delta).
- R3: SLO definitions. Support custom SLOs at tenant level (e.g., p95 <= 250ms, error_rate <= 0.5%). SLO evaluation should be configurable over sliding windows (1h, 24h, 30d).
- R4: Alerting and automations. Integrations with existing Alerting service to fire when tenant SLOs breach. Automations should be pluggable: notify, throttle, or apply fallback model_variant.
- R5: Metering export. Daily export in newline-delimited JSON (ndjson) to customer S3 or internal finance bucket with schema documented below.
- R6: Audit trails. All automated remediation actions must emit immutable audit records with initiator (system/rule/user), timestamp, and reason.

Non-functional requirements:
- NFR1: Control-plane overhead: per-tenant aggregation must not increase request path latency by more than 5 ms median.
- NFR2: Storage retention: telemetry stored for 90 days in hot storage, 13 months in cold.
- NFR3: Scalability: system must support 100k tenants with bursty traffic patterns (95th percentile tenant generates 50 req/s).
- NFR4: Privacy: default confidentiality is tenant-scoped; no customer prompt contents are stored unredacted unless customer opts in.

Metering export schema (ndjson; one record per tenant per day):
- Fields: date, tenant_id, customer_name, tokens_in, tokens_out, embedding_units, total_compute_seconds, committed_capacity_units, burst_credit_used, avg_p95_latency_ms, error_rate, region, model_family, billing_keys

Example record (ndjson):
{
  "date": "2026-11-19",
  "tenant_id": "acct_5aX2i",
  "customer_name": "Acme Retail",
  "tokens_in": "1,234,567",
  "tokens_out": "2,345,678",
  "embedding_units": "12,400",
  "total_compute_seconds": "452.3",
  "committed_capacity_units": "400",
  "burst_credit_used": "35",
  "avg_p95_latency_ms": "210",
  "error_rate": "0.003",
  "region": "us-west-2",
  "model_family": "rw-instruct-70b",
  "billing_keys": "route:chat-submit,project:checkout"
}

APIs and Console UX (sketch):
- GET /v1/tenants/{tenant_id}/metrics?start=2026-11-01T00:00Z&end=2026-11-20T23:59Z&granularity=1h -> returns paginated time-series of aggregated metrics.
- POST /v1/tenants/{tenant_id}/slos -> body: { "name": "checkout-p95", "metric": "p95_latency_ms", "threshold": 250, "window_mins": 60 }
- POST /v1/tenants/{tenant_id}/automation-rules -> body: { "trigger": "slo_breach", "action": "fallback_variant", "params": { "variant": "rw-instruct-7b-quant" } }

Console wireframes (text):
- Tenant Summary: header with committed capacity vs actual, sparkline for tokens, current p95, and a top-3 cost drivers list.
- SLO Heatmap: matrix of tenants x SLOs colored by health, filterable by region and model_family.
- Cost Drivers: sortable table of routes/prompts/feature flags with delta contribution to billing.

SLOs and thresholds (proposal):
- Site SLOs (default): p95_latency_ms <= 300ms, error_rate <= 1%.
- Dedicated tenant default: p95_latency_ms <= 250ms, error_rate <= 0.5%, throughput >= committed_capacity * 0.95.
- Enforcement: after 3 consecutive 5-minute windows of breach, automation rules trigger.

Policy actions and expected behavior:
1. Notify: send webhook/email to tenant owners and create internal incident if severity high.
2. Throttle: apply tenant-level token rate limiting to a target throughput (configurable).
3. Fallback: route matching requests to cheaper model_variant for a bounded time window and annotate traces.
4. Capacity escalation: if a tenant is within 10% of committed capacity for > 1 hour, auto-propose additional reserved capacity in console.

Pricing and packaging implications:
- New product offering: Tenant SLO Bundles. Each bundle ties a committed capacity (CU/month), an SLO tier (Standard/Enhanced/Premium), and burst credits. Pricing is additive: base committed price + SLO premium (e.g., Enhanced = +20% on commit).
- Metering keys introduced above will be used by billing: committed_capacity_units and burst_credit_used
- Implementation note: to avoid billing reconciliation churn, exports will include both raw units and pre-aggregated billable units; Finance will own mapping to invoice lines.

Rollout plan (phased):
Phase 0 (pilot, 2 weeks): implement per-tenant aggregation and daily ndjson export for 10 pilot customers; verify latency and storage costs.
Phase 1 (beta, 8 weeks): surface Console pages, allow rule creation for a restricted set of automations (notify & throttle), collect feedback.
Phase 2 (GA, 12 weeks): expose full automation set (fallback & capacity escalation), integrate with billing exports, and provide tenant CSVs for sales.
Phase 3 (post-GA): add ML-backed cost-driver attribution (advanced) and export hooks for third-party FinOps tools.

Operational runbook snippet (when SLOs breach):
1. Pagerless alerting to tenant owner and platform oncall.
2. Automated throttle applied if configured.
3. If throttle fails to bring SLO within range in 15 minutes, fallback to cheaper variant and create action item for capacity review.
4. Engineering oncall validates whether incident is system-wide or tenant-specific.

Acceptance criteria (must pass to ship GA):
- AC1: Telemetry pipeline emits complete per-tenant records for 99.9% of requests in pilot tenants.
- AC2: Console displays Tenant Summary and SLO Heatmap for pilot tenants with < 2s load time for dashboards.
- AC3: Automation rules execute within 10s of triggered condition and emit audit records.
- AC4: Metering export schema validated by Finance and SRE against 30 days of historical data.

Metrics to track post-launch:
- Adoption: #tenants with SLOs configured, #automation rules created.
- Reliability: percent of telemetry records delivered, average dashboard load time.
- Business: incremental committed capacity purchases attributed to feature, churn reduction for top-tier tenants.

Ownership and next steps:
- Product (Maya Chen): overall PM and roadmap.
- Eng (owner TBD): runtime aggregation, API endpoints, automations.
- Console UX (Alice Nguyen): dashboard and rule editor flows.
- Finance (Diego Morales): export schema sign-off and ingestion plan.

Open questions for PM/Eng review:
- Q1: Should SLO evaluation be performed in the control plane (near real-time) or asynchronously in a metrics pipeline? Trade-offs: real-time enables faster automation but increases control-plane cost.
- Q2: How granular should billing keys be (route-level vs feature flag)? More granularity improves attribution but increases cardinality and storage costs.
- Q3: Default retention policy for tenant telemetry: 90 days hot vs 365 days cold?

Appendix: example automation rule JSON (console editor payload)
```json
{
  "name": "checkout-fallback-on-p95-breach",
  "trigger": { "type": "slo_breach", "slo_name": "checkout-p95", "window_mins": 15 },
  "action": { "type": "fallback_variant", "params": { "variant": "rw-instruct-7b-quant", "duration_mins": 30 } },
  "conditions": { "min_requests": 100, "region": "us-*" }
}
```
